ex: He actually had - she was pregnant at the time, so now his daughter - his now - his daughter is basically the same age as he was when he went into the coma.

And um, he's just started coming around, he's just started making jokes. He said - they said, uh, "How do you feel?", he said "Horny." which I thought was quite witty for man who's been in a coma for, uh, many years. Um, but anyway, yeah…

q: Steve said he wouldn't want the job of a woman in a snack hut on Finchley Road. What was the problem?
a: She's so packed in with snacks she can't move
x: She has to eat whatever doesn't sell
She's not allowed to sit down
f: Steve: "She's got bananas up to her chin, just got chocolate coming down from her eyes, crisps either side of her. She can't move."
ex: And I don't know how to describe it really. She is surrounded by snacks. She can't move for snacks.
Does it look like American Beauty, but with with uh different
Not dissimilar to that it's a little hut on the station.

And it's like if you go to the seaside, you can put your head through one of those cardboard cutouts and it looks like you're a big fat person or whatever and you can have your photo taken. It's like an equivalent of that but it's just…

q: Steve wasn't sure whether to tip the man delivering his TV. What happened as the man left?
a: Steve reached for his ringing phone and the man held out his hand
x: Steve tipped him with a betting slip
The man asked for a fiver straight out
Steve gave him a bottle of wine by mistake
f: Steve: "he reached his hand out thinking it was a tip. I went 'oh, it's just my phone'."
ex: But the problem was, I didn't realize and I was thinking to myself "I wonder if I've got tip him" and the guy was leaving and my mobile phone went off in my pocket, and I reach in to get it, at he reached his hand out thinking it was a…
But I felt terrible after he left, I didn't know. What I was gonna do? Run down the street and offer him a fiver?

q: Steve said he genuinely couldn't see the appeal of Madame Tussauds. Whose waxwork did he give as his example?
a: J.Lo
f: Steve: "I just genuinely, with no irony, cannot see the appeal of having my photo taken next to a waxwork of J.Lo."
ex: Seems ill-informed. I can't think of many beyond anteater. You talked about— you're talking about the zoo though, I was watching the news last night and it had a feature about Madame Tussauds.

It was saying that they scrapped many of the royal family. Now, I don't— but I've never understood the appeal of Madame Tussauds. I just genuinely, with no irony, cannot see the appeal of having my photo taken next to a waxwork of J.Lo.
I can't compute why that would be fun. I don't know— what is it, do they
Move? Cause they don't move, do they?

q: What was Steve's advice to the woman advertising herself in The Stage as a Jordan look-alike?
a: Just become a Page 3 model herself
x: Get a proper job on the telly
Charge double for the real thing
f: Steve: "Stop pretending to be Jordan!" Ricky suggested she name herself after another Middle Eastern country.
ex: There was one at the back of The Stage that was "so-and-so... is Jordan", and it was a woman— a sort of buxom girl wearing very little.
Buxom! Are you from the West Country?
But I thought to myself, if you're willing to get your norks out pretending to be Jordan, just get 'em out and become a Page 3 model!

q: Steve wanted a workout video hosted by Elle Macpherson or Cindy Crawford. Whose did his housemate buy?
a: Helen from Big Brother's
f: His mate's excuse: "It was the cheapest one, Steve." Steve: "Thanks very much, mate."
ex: …a sort of hour-long workout. And I said to him, get one of the ones that’s hosted by like uhm…

…Elle Macpherson or Cindy Crawford, you know, you know, someone like that, someone sexy, right? So I swear to God, we went down this morning, we put it on, right? Just want you to picture this scene, right? It’s me, and my mate, in our…
…right? That was—“It was the cheapest one, Steve,” he told me. Thanks very much, mate.

q: A clean-cut Guns N' Roses fan Steve met on set ended up in a fight in the mosh pit at Donington. Why did he think he stood out?
a: He was the only one wearing a white T-shirt
x: He was the only one wearing a tie
He was the only one who knew the words
f: Ricky reckoned that's why they attacked him: "there's a termite in the nest!"
ex: …and he went, “I’d never bee—I’d never been to those live gigs before. And uh I was down in the mosh pit. Aw, man alive, I was down there and I’ll tell you this—have you been in a mosh pit?” I went, “No,” he went, “Ugh, it’s crazy down…
I was like, “Okay,” I could just imagine him tucked in… as well… jeans…
That’s why, that’s why they attacked him.
Yeah. Slash himself said, “Get the tall…!”
Yeah yeah, there’s a termite in the nest!

q: What happened the one time the girl walked in on teenage Steve reading his philosophy book?
a: She said "Oh, sorry. Wrong room" and left
x: She asked if she could borrow it
She fetched his rival to laugh at him
She asked him to explain it to her
f: Steve: "And that was it!" Ricky had guessed Steve thought he was Kwai Chang Caine.
ex: I bet you thought you were Kwai Chang Caine, didn’t you?
I-I thought it was like she’d think, “Jesus Christ, I’ve never, I’ve never met anyone like him.”
And she- I remember the one time she accidentally walked in she went, “Oh! Oh, sorry. Wrong room.” and left again.

q: Karl said he'd come in specially on his days off to sort out the prizes. Where did Steve suggest he'd actually got them?
a: By rifling through the drawers up at Capital Gold
x: From the lost property box at reception
f: Karl's reply: "Yeh. Yeah." He said he'd only had three days off because he'd been "workin' all over Christmas".
ex: You've got a nice load of prizes there--
That I've sorted out. I had to come in here especially to sort that out.
Did you rifle through the drawers up at Capital Gold instead of down here?
Yeh. Yeah. Uhh, "Rockbusters" - we're still doin' that.

q: How did Steve hypothetically plan to get onto a nudist beach without stripping at the door?
a: Swim up to it in a wetsuit
x: Dig a tunnel under the dunes
Hide in an ice cream van
f: Steve's "fairly good swimmer" had time on his hands for a week. Ricky's twist: he was swimming there "From France!"
ex: Would it be possible for a bloke who was, say, a fairly good swimmer to swim up to the beach in a wetsuit--
Just say, just say for the sake of it that this person, you know, had some time on his hands for a week.

q: What was the only thing that spoiled Prince's nearly three-hour gig for Steve?
a: Being preached at about Prince's Jehovah's Witness beliefs
x: The sound was awful at the back
Prince stopped for a twenty-minute tea break
f: Steve had "paid forty quid" and sat for three hours "to then be preached at a little bit."
ex: He’s now a Jehovah’s Witness so--
And he’s going to come around tonight.
Well, no, but at the end he did sort of spout on about, uh, you know, his beliefs.
Uh, and I felt a bit like I’d, d'you know what I mean, like I’d, sort of, paid forty quid and I’d queued up and I’d sat for three hours to then--
To then, to then be preached at a little bit. So that was the only thing that-that put that down for me.

q: Callers could only half-remember the 'people eater' song. Which DJ did Steve wish would ring in with the full details?
a: Paul Gambaccini
f: Steve wanted someone who knew "what chart position it got to". He told callers: "Have all the facts at hand!"
ex: This is not enough information! I wouldn't phone in if I didn't- have half the information!
We didn't ask him who- we asked him just what the tune was!
But I want someone like Paul Gambaccini (Laughing Slightly) to call in. He knows what- you know, what chart position it got to...
Well, okay, okay, right. Thanks very much--
I don't think this is enough information! That's two people, we barely got any information!

q: Steve read about a man who died falling out of a window while mooning. What did he say would have been a better last gag to die after?
a: A two-hour impromptu Eddie Izzard-style routine
x: A whoopee cushion at a wedding
f: Ricky: "Mooning isn't funny enough." Steve: "It's just not a good enough gag." He called the death "almost karmic".
ex: No. It's just not a good enough gag.
Do you know what I mean? It's a witless sort of thing to do and then to be killed for it.
If you just done a two hour impromptu Eddie Izard-style routine and then you got tragically killed, that would sort of make sense.
But mooning, it's almost karmic because it's such a bad joke.

q: Steve pointed out a monkey's testicle is big for a mouse. What did he think the mouse would look like it was sitting on?
a: A space hopper
f: Karl agreed it wasn't a good look: "Oh yeah, it didn't look good."
ex: But isn't it-- I mean, a monkey's testicle quite large in relation to a mouse? Would it not look like the mouse was on a Space hopper or something?
Oh yeah, it didn't look good.

q: In the pool hall, an uncle bumped a baby's head on a chair and then told the mum he didn't know what happened. What did Steve want to say?
a: "You lying swine"
f: Steve's other thought about the baby: "who knows, he might turn out like Karl now."
ex: They sit down, and the weirdest thing was one of the kids, one of the guys, the uncle, let's say, of the fete, he picked up the kid and he put, he's about to put the baby down in a chair. And I thought, hang on that's quite, quite a…

And it started screaming and crying, you know, and the teenagers were rocking to that, they loved it, and um and it came over, and it was transparent what had happened, and the mom was going "What's happened, the baby's crying!"
And he went, "I don't know what happened." And I wanted to lean over and go, "You lying swine".
"When you just hit his head" I wanted to go, just take her aside and say, "never let him handle your baby again".
No, The head was wobbling around, and I could see it coming.
I don't know, who knows, he might turn out like Karl now.

q: Listener Alexandra sent Karl a packet of Fox's biscuits to save him money. What did Steve suggest he do with them?
a: Wrap them up and give them to his girlfriend
x: Send them to Suzanne's dad for his birthday
Offer them as a Rockbusters prize
Sell them to Ricky at cost price
f: A dig at Karl having no present for Suzanne. The biscuits were later eaten during a record, earning Karl's review: "Good, that."
ex: We've also a lovely Christmas card here, from Alexandra, right, who's, uhh, wish us a l- she loves the show, she loves you, Karl, and she's enclosed some biscicks- biscuits for ya to save you a bit of money cuz she knows you go out and get…
Well why don't you wrap them up and you can give them to your girlfriend.

q: Steve insisted Leona Lewis went on The X Factor to sing, and not because she fancied working down a branch of which shop?
a: Waterstones
f: Karl wasn't convinced and said she "might have had a backup plan!"
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The Future · 2009
ex: Yeah, but we don't know what Leona wanted to do, she might have a backup plan.
She might have had a backup plan!
Yeah but she fulfilled the main ambition, which was to sing! That's why she went on the show! She didn't go there because she thought "Oh, I might want to work down a branch of Waterstones"
You think she went in there and said "Quarter of bom-boms" (mumbles) "This is X-Factor." And she went "Oh, go on then."

q: Ricky told Karl how King Solomon offered to cut a disputed baby in half. What did Steve say the lying woman should have said instead?
a: "Yeah, give it to the other one as well."
f: Steve felt the liar blew it: she "could have come up with something better than, 'Yeah, cut it in half!'" Karl's own reaction to the story: "So which one was it?"
ex: Although it's not a very good solution.
No, that doesn't make any sense.
The woman who was lying could have come up with something better than, "Yeah, cut it in half!"
What she should have done is, "Yeah, give it to the other one as well."

q: Hearing that Auntie Nora mashes up leftovers and keeps them in tubs in the fridge, what did Steve first assume?
a: She kept them as a souvenir of each meal she'd had
x: She was saving them to feed the cat
She was saving them for when Karl came round
She was sending them off to be tested
f: Karl corrected him: "No, put it in a pan. Warm it up." Steve: "Oh, that's grotesque."
ex: Put it in the fridge. And she's got in the fridge, it's like January, February, March. She's got all these ice cream boxes that are just full of--
But she doesn't- she reheats it and eats it?
Oh, the- then she, yeah, puts it in the pan.
I thought she was keeping it as a souvenir--
No, put it in a pan. Warm it up.

q: Steve said he'd never have gone to see a film starring Clive Warren and Rebecca De Mornay, unless what?
a: It was 1985
f: Steve had already pointed out De Mornay "hasn't been in a film for 15 years". And Clive Warren doesn't exist.
ex: I'd have switched off. But yeah.
No you wouldn't, this, this bit would have you. So what-
Well, I'd have actually left when I, I wouldn't have even gone in to see a film starring Clive Warren and Rebecca De Mornay. Unless, unless it was 1985.
So the thing is, she's the same as you. She says the same thing. She goes "Why would I do that doctor?"

q: Listeners emailed asking Ricky and Steve to stop calling Karl stupid. Which Karl idea did Steve offer as proof that he could be called stupid?
a: Injecting a 76-year-old woman in the head so she lives backwards
x: Freezing his dad so he can be thawed out in 100 years
Shrinking a pensioner so she fits in a smaller house
Teaching a goldfish to whistle so it's less lonely
f: Steve didn't see what part of "injecting a 76 year old woman in the head so that she lives her life backwards" couldn't be considered stupid.
ex: Well, can I just ask because there's been an awful lot of emails that have said, "will you and Steve please stop calling Karl stupid".
Now they say, oh, it doesn't, just doesn't justify calling him stupid. Now I don't know what part of injecting a 76 year old woman in the head so that she lives her life backwards--

q: Steve ran a mobile disco from about 14 to 18. What was its original name, before it became "The Fantasy Island Roadshow"?
a: The Rock and Roll DJs
f: Ricky's verdict on "The Rock and Roll DJs": "that's the worst." Steve admitted it got "pretty bad after that" too.
ex: It started its life as... bear with it--
Oh my god... "The Rock and Roll DJ"... that's the worst...
Yeah. That's the most appalling. But then, it became pretty bad after that... when it became... "The Fantasy Island Roadshow"

q: Watching a mid-80s Family Fortunes repeat, Steve mocked a contestant's hobby. What was it?
a: Going out when it's nice and staying in when it's not
x: Feeding the ducks in the park
f: Steve on such dreams: "you're just waiting to die, aren't you." Karl on Family Fortunes: "Oh I hate that."
ex: Well it's interesting, 'cause I wonder sometimes what your aspirations are. I was thinking this, I was watching uh, a repeat of 'Family Fortunes', on Challenge TV last night...

...and it was sort of mid-eighties one, and I don't know if it's still the case but it was the aspirations of the contestants, were so kind of, it was like "and what's your hobby?", "Well, you know, I like to go out when it's nice weather…
"Well if you win two thousand pounds you can probably be going out, when it's nice, couldn't you?", "Yeah".

And she was like, "Well, and I, you know, I sometimes like to watch TV, you know", and I was thinking, wow, man, you've really got some incredible dreams there. It's just like that, I'm--you're just waiting to die, aren't you, that's all…

q: Steve said "The Smiths" was a genius band name. What did he say it captured?
a: That mediocre world of grim up-northness
x: The clang of a blacksmith's forge
The smell of a Manchester chippy
f: Steve said the name "sums up everything that band is about" and that it proves there's "some logic" to band names.
ex: But my point is people say there’s no logic to band names, but if you think of a band name like “The Smiths”…
It sums up everything that band is about, you know, the kind of, they’re capturing that mediocre world of grim up-northness, you know.
